meta.subtitle: How the multi-domain, multi-language glossary registry works. File layout, project-level overrides, disambiguation, the resolution algorithm.
meta.summary: Multi-domain glossary architecture and how to extend it.

blocks.summary: Glossary and ext-ref entries live in per-domain files under _kit/glossary/ and _kit/extrefs/. Each project's kit.json activates a subset of domains in priority order and can add local overrides. Resolution walks active domains, falls back through preferred languages, surfaces unknowns via the forward-compat warning indicator.
bullets: Per-domain files — separate ACID in data-platforms from ACID in chemistry, separate RSD in adhd from RSD in radio.
Per-entry multi-language variants — { "en": {...}, "tr": {...} }. The canonical link can differ per language.
Project kit.json declares active domains + preferred language + project-local entries. Local entries always win on conflict.
Unknown terms surface in the forward-compat warning indicator; add the entry to project kit.json or push to central.

blocks.title: File layout
blocks.lead: Central glossaries ship with the kit; projects extend via kit.json or by adding their own domain files.

blocks.source:
oku/                          # the kit repo
├── glossary/
│   ├── data-platforms.json
│   ├── web.json
│   ├── ai-llm.json
│   ├── adhd.json    (structural stub — populate as needed)
│   ├── hadith.json
│   └── voice.json
├── extrefs/
│   ├── doc-tooling.json
│   ├── data-platforms.json
│   ├── web.json
│   └── ai-llm.json
└── ...

your-project/
└── docs/
    ├── _kit -> /path/to/oku   # symlink
    ├── kit.json                    # active domains + overrides
    ├── page-a.html / page-a.json
    └── ...

blocks.title: Entry shape
blocks.lead: Each entry is a dict of language → { def, link }. def supports inline HTML (strong, em, br, code) because it's rendered as the tooltip body. The trust boundary is documented in chrome.js — kit-controlled files only.

blocks.title: ext-refs use the same shape
blocks.content: _kit/extrefs/<domain>.json uses identical structure — each entry has language variants with name, summary, link. Same resolution algorithm, separate registry.

blocks.title: Project configuration — kit.json
blocks.lead: Each project's docs/kit.json declares which domains are active and in what priority order, the preferred language with fallback chain, and any local additions or overrides.

blocks.summary: Local entries always win on conflict

content: When the same term appears in both
, the project version is used. Merge happens after the central file loads, so a project override is never silently discarded by a later registry fetch.

blocks.title: Disambiguation — same term, different domains
blocks.lead: When two active domains define the same term, the author can qualify with the in attribute. Default behavior is "first matching domain wins" so most usage is unqualified.

blocks.source:
// In page JSON, inside a paragraph.content array:
{ "kind": "glossary-term", "term": "ACID" }                       // first match wins
{ "kind": "glossary-term", "term": "ACID", "in": "chemistry" }    // explicit
{ "kind": "glossary-term", "term": "ACID", "lang": "tr" }         // override language

content: attribute restricts lookup to one domain even if it's not first in the project's domains list. The
attribute overrides the project's preferred language for that instance — useful when one term in a TR-default project needs an English-source citation.

blocks.title: Resolution algorithm
blocks.lead: Implemented in chrome.js as __okuKit.resolveGlossary and resolveExtRef.

steps.title: Domain selection
steps.content: If the in attribute is set, lookup is restricted to that one domain. Otherwise walk the project's domains array in declared order.

steps.title: Per-domain lookup
steps.content: For each candidate domain, check project-local overrides first, then the central _kit/glossary/<domain>.json. First match wins.

steps.title: Language pick
steps.content: Try the preferred language (from lang attribute or kit.json's lang). If absent, walk kit.json's lang_fallback list. If still absent, use the first available language and mark data-lang-shown so the tooltip displays the actual language tag.

steps.title: Unknown — surface a warning
steps.content: If no entry found anywhere, emit an unknown-glossary-term (or unknown-ext-ref) warning event. The forward-compat indicator counts it; the element gets the .unknown class with amber-dotted styling.

blocks.title: Adding new entries
blocks.lead: Two paths — project-local for quick iteration, central PR when the term proves general.

cards.title: Project-local first
cards.content: Add to your project's docs/kit.json under glossary[<domain>][<term>]. Takes effect immediately. No commits to the kit needed. Works for project-specific terms and quick experimentation.

cards.title: Promote to central
cards.content: When a term proves general (used in two or three projects, or clearly belongs in the domain), commit it to _kit/glossary/<domain>.json. Remove the project-local copy when central lands.

blocks.title: Forward-compat warning surfaces unknowns
blocks.content: When the AI emits a term that's not in any active domain, the warning indicator lights up with code: "unknown-glossary-term". Click to see the missing entry name. Fast feedback that an addition is overdue.

blocks.title: Bundled starter content
blocks.lead: Three domains arrive populated; three are empty structural stubs ready to fill in.

cards.title: Populated
items: data-platforms — ACID, MVCC, Iceberg, Spark, Flink, Paimon, Catalog, Snapshot, Compaction, Time travel (with TR translations on the most common)
web — Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, FOUC, Viewport, Visual Viewport, prefers-color-scheme, localStorage, History API, IntersectionObserver, CSS variable
ai-llm — RAG, Tokenization, Prompt cache, Context window, Embedding, Vector DB, Function calling, Hallucination, Few-shot, Top-k / Top-p

cards.title: Structural stubs
items: adhd — populate with RSD, hyperfocus, executive dysfunction, etc.
hadith — populate with isnad, matn, sahih, da'if, etc.
voice — populate with phoneme, prosody, formant, etc.
Add new domains by dropping a new <domain>.json file in glossary/ and listing it in your project's kit.json
